claims.text: The relevant HfNbTaTiZr material is a concentrated, single-phase alloy.
HfNbTaTiZr specimens with about 1 wt.% oxygen can be regarded as nearly defect-free.
The proposed framework explicitly models atomic disorder and anharmonic phonon scattering.
The proposed framework separately accounts for lattice and electronic thermal transport.
The proposed framework does not rely on a Debye-temperature approximation.
Atomic-scale compositional disorder mediates phonon scattering in HfNbTaTiZr.
Anharmonic vibrational modes mediate phonon scattering in HfNbTaTiZr.
Capturing compositional disorder and strong anharmonic interactions enables proper separation of lattice and electronic thermal-transport contributions.
Moving beyond idealized bulk-crystal assumptions reduces discrepancies relative to Debye- or elastic-modulus-based approaches.
The new approach will predict the isolated lattice thermal conductivity within approximately ±15–20% over 300–1200 K.
The new approach will be more accurate than prior Debye- or elastic-property-scaling methods.
Earlier analytical approaches have errors of approximately 50% or more.
The proposed model is primarily applicable to HfNbTaTiZr between 300 and 1200 K.
Lattice thermal transport dominates in HfNbTaTiZr over 300–1200 K.
Separation of lattice and electronic transport is clearer over 300–1200 K than below 200 K.
Below 200 K, lattice and electronic contributions in HfNbTaTiZr are comparable and therefore harder to isolate.
Impurity levels substantially above the controlled low-oxygen condition introduce additional thermal scattering and may invalidate the prediction.
Sample purity and measurement technique can affect the observed predictive accuracy.
Electrical-conductivity measurements combined with the Wiedemann–Franz law can be used to estimate and subtract the electronic thermal-conductivity contribution.
